reading.body:
Equinix DC2 is a 118,446 square foot facility in Ashburn, Virginia with N+1 redundancy in both power and cooling, plus 30 hours of generator autonomy at full load. The operator does not publish a megawatt capacity for this building, so its actual power draw cannot be compared directly to other facilities or summed into regional totals. At a typical AI training density of 40 kilowatts per rack, even a modest 10 megawatts of IT load would support roughly 250 racks, but without published figures this remains speculative.

DC2 is one of 15 facilities Equinix operates across the Washington DC metropolitan region, which the operator positions as North America's largest peering point and a major gateway to Europe. Virginia overall has 326 mapped data centers, only 23 of which publish power capacity figures to this site, accounting for 1,375 megawatts total. Because DC2's capacity is unpublished, it does not rank within that 23-facility cohort.

The absence of a published megawatt figure for this building is itself significant. Equinix publishes capacity selectively across its metro portfolio, leaving most of its individual facility power consumption opaque to independent capacity tracking. This means DC2's role in Virginia's data center footprint, and its relevance to grid constraints on AI scaling, cannot be assessed from public sources.
